title: Culinary Classroom
before:
If you have questions regarding the Culinary Classroom, please contact a member of the Child Nutrition staff. 

Recipes, Tips & Ideas from the Culinary Classroom

Looking for some new recipe ideas? Want to make things in your kitchen more efficient?
Check out the videos and recipes that come straight from the Child Nutrition Culinary Classroom. 


Will you be coming to the Culinary Classroom? Please read the information below. 

 

Classroom Dress Code

All participants and presenters participating in training events held in the Culinary Classroom will be required to follow our dress code. The following standards must be met:

  • A hat or hairnet is required. Other head coverings with prior approval may be allowed. Visors are not allowed.
  • Beard restraint, if applicable
  • Closed-toe/back shoes
  • Long pants, no leggings
  • Short or long sleeve shirts only
  • A plain wedding band is the only jewelry allowed
  • Nails must be clean and trimmed. Nail polish and artificial nails will not be allowed.


Participation

We ask that the following order be adhered to for those who wish to participate:

  • Cooks and Prep Cooks
  • Directors and Managers who work or assist in the kitchen
  • Non-production staff

Participation Agreement

To participate in our culinary training, participants must sign a Participation Agreement before the training. Please read, sign, and email the completed form to Paula Nadeau at paula.nadeau@maine.gov 

Cancellation Policy

In the event of inclement weather, a decision will be made by noon the day before the training as to whether or not the training will take place.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 3 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Recipes, Tips & Ideas from the Culinary Clas" is an h5 with no h4 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Participation Agreement" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Cancellation Policy" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 3 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — paula.nadeau@maine.gov → Paula.Nadeau@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 6 links on this page open a file — 5 PDF, 1 Video — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 2 sub-headings are plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.

decisions.label: Jumbotron callouts become notes
decisions.why: 1 callout is built as a Bootstrap jumbotron, which the component list replaced with dc-note and which Bootstrap itself removed in version 5. Same content, the site's own callout.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Left-align a section header
decisions.why: 3 section headers are centred, where 1,103 of the 1,139 on the site are left-aligned — the component list says not to centre them. The band runs the full width of the column, so a centred title has no fixed relationship to anything else, and a two-line one breaks the left edge every other heading shares. Only the alignment changes.

decisions.label: Run a label into the line it labels
decisions.why: 1 label sits alone in a paragraph with the sentence it labels in the next one — two blocks, two margins and a line break to say one thing. Down a list of exclusions that reads as a column of orphaned labels. Run in with a colon, which is how a term and its definition are set. The only character added is the colon.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Size an image by its shape
decisions.why: "Food Safety Timeline" measures 3000×2250 — it was sitting in the flow at its own pixel size, aligned with nothing.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (3 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.

decisions.label: Draw the contact sentence as a contact block
decisions.why: The page carries a sentence whose whole job is to say who to ask, set as body text at the top where it is read before anything it could answer. Drawn as the site's contact block at the foot it sits where a reader looks for it, and the banner gains the Contact chip that jumps to it. The sentence and its link are unchanged.
